claim: The most-cited 2024 Southeast Asia influencer-marketing sector report contains no creator-side survey at all: its only quantified instrument is a demand-side consumer survey (n=2,400), so it supplies zero SEA data on creator income distribution, attrition, or time-to-first-income.
stance_target: The claim that quantitative creator-attrition and creator-income evidence for Southeast Asia is essentially absent, and that SEA-labelled reports actually measure consumers or brands rather than creators
scope_conditions: Southeast Asia (Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Philippines); fieldwork June-August 2024; vendor/agency report sponsored by impact.com
quoted_support: Online consumer survey of 2,400 respondents (adults aged 18-77, men and women), focused on sentiments towards influencers and influencer marketing. Singapore (n=400) Indonesia (n=400) Thailand (n=400) Vietnam (n=400) Malaysia (n=400) Philippines (n=400)

claim: Supply-side findings in the report rest on in-depth interviews with influencers, brand marketers and agencies for which no sample size is disclosed anywhere in the document.
stance_target: The claim that SEA creator-economy figures in circulation lack traceable methodology and cannot be treated as quantitative evidence
scope_conditions: Southeast Asia; 2024 report; methodology page states three instruments (expert interviews, Cube market data, consumer survey) and gives an N only for the last
quoted_support: In-depth interviews with industry stakeholders and experts including influencers, brand marketing leaders, and representatives from enablers and agencies.

claim: Total e-commerce marketing expenditure on influencers across six Southeast Asian countries is estimated at approximately $5bn in 2024, of which influencer fees are about 60%, implying a regional cash fee pool of roughly $3bn.
stance_target: Sizing the total revenue available to Southeast Asian creators from e-commerce influencer marketing, as a denominator for per-creator income estimates
scope_conditions: Six SEA countries; 2024 forecast; proprietary Cube estimates from brand/e-commerce leader survey and interviews plus desktop research; excludes platform ad-revenue share and non-commerce brand deals
quoted_support: E-commerce marketing expenditure on influencers will reach ~$5bn in 2024 ... Influencer fees fixed fees, sales commission, travel expenses ~60%

claim: Payment-in-kind is a standing structural feature of Southeast Asian influencer marketing: smaller-following influencers often receive free products as their sole remuneration, and brands routinely seed product to more than 100 influencers per campaign.
stance_target: The claim that a large share of the creator long tail earns zero cash income, so headline creator counts vastly overstate the number of paid creators
scope_conditions: Southeast Asia; 2024; based on brand/e-commerce leader survey, influencer interviews and expert interviews with no disclosed sample size
quoted_support: Influencers, especially those with a smaller following, often receive free products as the sole remuneration for their work ... savvy brands often seed free product to >100 influencers per campaign
numbers: product sponsorship = ~25% of influencer marketing spend

claim: A study of 371 products on the TikTok Shop open-affiliate marketplace in August 2024 found average affiliate commission rates of 9% overall, ranging 1-35%, with sellers permitted to set anywhere from 1% to 80%.
stance_target: Establishing the per-sale unit economics that determine how much gross merchandise value a Southeast Asian affiliate creator must generate to earn a given income
scope_conditions: TikTok Shop open affiliate marketplace, Southeast Asia, August 2024; observational study of 371 listed products
quoted_support: Commission rates on TikTok range around 1% to 35% across the top categories. Fashion products have the highest commission rates, averaging at 10%, followed by beauty at 9% and electronics at 8%

claim: TikTok Shop live streamers in Southeast Asia are paid on a hybrid model averaging 9% affiliate commission on generated sales, plus a fixed hourly appearance fee and free product.
stance_target: Characterising the composition of Southeast Asian creator income as commission-weighted rather than salaried or ad-revenue-share weighted
scope_conditions: TikTok Shop live commerce, Southeast Asia, 2024; from brand and e-commerce leader survey and expert interviews
quoted_support: The live streamer receives on average 9% of generated sales as affiliate commission; products are shipped directly from brand warehouse
numbers: commissions most commonly 10-30% per report text

claim: Influencer marketing directly generated an estimated $15bn of the $149bn Southeast Asian formal-channel e-commerce market in 2024 (about 10%), with total influenced sales of $25-31bn (17-21%).
stance_target: Sizing the commercial importance of the creator channel in Southeast Asia relative to Western markets
scope_conditions: Six SEA countries; 2024 forecast; proprietary Cube estimates, methodology not disclosed; excludes cancellations and returns
quoted_support: Influencer marketing is a significant sales driver for e-commerce in Southeast Asia, directly contributing ~$15bn of NMV in 2024

claim: Southeast Asian consumer demand for influencer content is high and rising -- 82% of surveyed consumers report purchasing on an influencer recommendation -- while the average number of influencers followed fell from 26 to 23 year on year, indicating audience attention consolidating rather than expanding.
stance_target: The assumption that strong consumer engagement with influencers in SEA implies a proportionally expanding number of viable creator careers
scope_conditions: Consumer survey n=2,400 across six SEA countries, August 2024; self-reported purchase behaviour, subject to recall bias
quoted_support: 82% of respondents have purchased a product that was recommended by an influencer; this is a +3% increase versus 2023 ... On average, consumers follow 23 influencers; this is 3 fewer than our survey in 2023

claim: Influencer recommendation power varies sharply within Southeast Asia -- Thailand 69% versus Singapore 41% -- so single-region SEA generalisations conceal a 28-point spread between member countries.
stance_target: The claim that 'Southeast Asia' is not a single market for creator economics and that country-level disaggregation is required
scope_conditions: Consumer survey n=400 per country, August 2024; measures share rating influencer recommendations as positive or very positive for purchase decisions
quoted_support: Thailand has the highest influencer recommendation power and has seen the highest rise since 2023, up 7% ... In contrast, Singapore has experienced the largest decline in influencer recommendation power, down 8% from the previous year
